title: Negotiation signal cards — quick phrasing and clause priorities
summary: Pocket reference for fast counterparty calls. Short, color-coded lines to use live (or drop into chat) plus prioritized clause list and fallback math. Designed for last-minute prep or as a crib sheet for SEs who need one-line positions.
signal_cards: Green — We accept the clause as-is (minor edits only). Move forward; flag for post-signature operational note.
Yellow — We want a change but can accept a compromise: propose a time- or scope-limited concession (e.g., pilot-only data residency, or probationary support SLA).
Red — Non-starter without material change (use only when legal/ops would block). Offer explicit alternative or walkaway point.
Data residency — Yellow: 90 days to provide region residency plan; Green if customer accepts transient processing in a supported region + written SOC/ISO attestations.
Liability cap — Red: unlimited or open-ended; Counter: 2x fees in previous 12 months OR $1M (whichever is greater) — explain with dollars, not abstract language.
Indemnity — Yellow: carve out TLS/OSS/third-party model risk; Green if mutual indemnity for IP infringement with standard exclusions.
Audit/request access — Yellow: propose scoped audit window + 30 days' notice + redaction and co-located observer option; Green: SOC/ISO reports accepted in lieu of on-site audit.
Escrow — Green: offer escrow for model binary + critical config for enterprise + customer-paid escrow admin fees; Red if they demand live sync or superuser rights.
Termination for convenience — Yellow: accept with 60–90 days transition assistance and prorated refund of prepaid fees; Red if they demand immediate cutover or data handoff without compensation.
Export/control language — Red: any clause that prevents us from serving other customers or shipping minor updates; Counter with narrowly tailored export compliance language.
SLA credits — Green if credits limited and not sole remedy; Red if they try to tee up credits that reduce liability caps or create service-level penalties that exceed cap.
Support & incident response — Green: 24-48h standard; Yellow: faster SLAs for paid support tier only; Counter with runbook + RTO/RPO only for critical incidents.
Data deletion/return — Green: certified deletion within agreed window (30–90d); Yellow if they ask for prolonged retention — propose encrypted escrow + documented access list.
IP assignment — Red for blanket assignment of improvements; Counter with license-back to us for improvements that are product-agnostic and not customer-specific.
Confidentiality carve-outs — Yellow: allow necessary operational disclosures to SRE/infra and auditors under NDA; Green if mutual and time-limited.
Warranty scope — Yellow: limited to conformity with docs and not for model hallucination; Green if explicit exclusions for emergent LLM behaviors are included.
red_flags: Unlimited liability or unspecified 'gross negligence' threshold — immediate escalation.
Perpetual IP assignment for derivative outputs of the model — push back hard.
Broad audit rights without scope or notice — operationally infeasible.
Data residency as a contractual perpetual obligation without ops timeline — negotiate phased approach.
Termination that forces immediate downtime and no transition assistance — commercial risk.
Reverse indemnities that attempt to shift product defects onto us for 3rd-party models or upstream data.
phrase_snippets: Counterproposal: liability shall be limited to the greater of (a) two times the fees paid to Supplier under the applicable Order in the 12 months prior to the claim, or (b) one million US dollars (USD 1,000,000).

Data processing: Supplier may process Customer data in locations consistent with Supplier's published region map; Supplier will provide SOC2/ISO attestations on request. Customer may request region-specific deployment for an agreed surcharge and lead time of 60 days.

Audit: Customer may request one remote compliance review per 12-month period with 30 days' notice; onsite audits require mutual agreement and Customer reimbursement of reasonable travel and administrative costs.

Escrow: For enterprise plans, Supplier will deposit in escrow the required deliverables limited to the model artifacts necessary to restore service; Customer shall pay escrow administration and retrieval fees.

Termination assistance: Upon termination for convenience, Supplier will provide knowledge transfer and data export assistance for up to 90 days subject to mutually agreed SOW; fees prorated for prepaid service periods.
concession_ladder: 1) Clarify ambiguous language (narrow scope) — smallest ask.
2) Propose time-bound or tiered obligations (pilot -> enterprise) — operational compromise.
3) Offer contractual SLA in exchange for liability cap retention (trade credit for cap relief).
4) For high-risk customers, require additional commercial protections (higher fees, escrow, longer notice periods).
5) Last resort: express walkaway language and get sales sign-off before conceding.
math_cheat: Liability cap heuristic: prefer formula 'max(2x last-12-mo fees, $1M)'. Explaining in $ terms helps non-legal PMs.
Audit window: 1 audit/12 months, 30 days' notice — calculate team bandwidth ~ 1–2 FTE-days prep + 1/2 day review.
Data residency cost: expect ~8–12 week infra lead time + up to 20% uplift on hosting for region isolation for initial migration.
negotiation_tips: Use plain-English one-liners in early meetings; keep legal quotes for tracked redlines only.
When pushed on a red flag, ask the use-case and quantify risk — often they accept a narrower scope.
Offer options: 'We can do A if you accept X; or we can do B with no additional terms' — gives control back to you.
Loop in solutions / SRE early if they ask for live access or operational playbooks; technical pushback is faster than legal-only rebuttal.
If customer demands high-risk language, tie concessions to commercial uplift (discount reduction or implementation fee).
fallback_positions: Require mutual indemnity for IP claims and carve-outs for OSS and third-party models.
Liability cap at formula above; absolute walkaway if counterparty insists on uncapped direct damages tied to deliverables we don't control.
Scoped audit or SOC/ISO reports accepted in lieu of on-site deep-dive.
Data export/deletion: certified deletion within 45 days or agreed transitional storage fee.
